item.title: CaptionForge 1.0.11
item.description:
Continuous captions, a reliable editable-title alternative, and motion for every style.

  • Keep captions continuous — With Continuous captions enabled, each title lasts until the next title begins, including one-word captions and word-by-word display. Speech starts, text and grouping stay intact; the final single word retains its audio end. Turn continuity off to preserve pauses.
  • Open separate editable titles — If Final Cut disables Break Apart, use the arrow beside Captions ready → Open separate titles in Final Cut…. Choose a library and open the imported project, copy its entire timeline, then use Edit → Paste as Connected Clip at your original audio’s start. This route needs no Timeline Helper or Accessibility permission. Direct dragging still inserts a group first.
  • Choose motion for any preset — Each of the twelve looks has its own default motion. In More settings, choose directional fly-ins, fades, zooms, pops, bounces and word highlights independently of the visual preset. Animate captions switches everything off while keeping your choices saved.
  • JGL Pop In — The signature entrance starts at 80% on frame 1, reaches 110% on frame 3 and settles at 100% on frame 4. Apply it to any preset. Captions shorter than four frames remain static so animation never extends their timing. Motion blur is not included.
  • Keep your existing setup — Quit Final Cut before installing, then reopen Window → Extensions → CaptionForge and confirm version 1.0.11 in the gear menu. Captions, named presets, font, size, X/Y position, colors and downloaded models stay saved. This remains a free friends beta; individual recordings may need corrections.

Quit Final Cut before updating. Captions, settings and downloaded models are preserved.

item.title: CaptionForge 1.0.10
item.description:
Independent X and Y controls that center your captions precisely.

  • Center either axis — Press the reset beside Position Y to center captions vertically, or the reset beside Position X to center horizontally. Each returns its axis to 50% of the video frame without changing the other axis, font, size or colors. Reset both to center the caption block.
  • Adjust Position X — Move captions horizontally with the new Position X slider. Double-click the X or Y number to type a precise position. Natural-phrase safe-area limits keep captions inside the frame at the selected font size.
  • Keep your positioning — X and Y are saved with your draft and named presets and restore when you reopen CaptionForge. Older projects without an X value remain horizontally centered. Preview and Final Cut export use matching positioning in portrait and landscape, including slide animations.
  • Update the same Final Cut extension — Close Final Cut before installation, then reopen Window → Extensions → CaptionForge and confirm version 1.0.10 in Settings. The existing timeline-delivery fix is retained. Saved captions, presets, settings and downloaded models stay in place.

Quit Final Cut before updating. Captions, settings and downloaded models are preserved.

item.title: CaptionForge 1.0.9
item.description:
A timeline-delivery fix for caption drops that Final Cut could not separate.

  • A proper caption compound — New drops use an explicit Final Cut compound clip containing the editable titles. Separate editable titles still inserts the group first, then Timeline Helper separates it. Keep grouped remains available. Caption text, styling and timing are preserved.
  • Replace an older drop — Updating cannot change a clip already on your timeline. If Final Cut disables Break Apart for an older CaptionForge drop, remove only that caption group and drag it again from the updated extension with Separate editable titles selected.
  • Clearer helper recovery — Timeline Helper distinguishes a disabled command, a changed selection and unavailable English menus. It also recognizes when Final Cut merges CaptionForge’s transparent background gaps, avoiding a false failure after successful separation. Close the setup window to quit the helper. Accessibility approval is still required on each Mac.
  • Update your existing extension — Close Final Cut before installing, then reopen Window → Extensions → CaptionForge and confirm version 1.0.9 in Settings. Saved captions, presets, appearance settings and downloaded models stay in place.

Quit Final Cut before updating. Captions, settings and downloaded models are preserved.

item.title: CaptionForge 1.0.8
item.description:
Clearer audio import and caption readiness, flexible timeline delivery, and reliable one-word export.

  • Know when you are ready — Imported audio shows its filename. Analyze is clearly highlighted when available, progress is visible, and completed captions show their count and readiness to drag.
  • One word works too — Very short single-word captions no longer block export. Each stays one editable title, with at least one video frame. Original text and audio timestamps stay unchanged; the timing summary lists frame adjustments.
  • Remove all punctuation — Remove punctuation in More settings for cleaner captions. Preview, titles and SRT update together, and switching it off restores your original transcript.
  • Your choice on the timeline — Choose Keep grouped or Separate editable titles from the drag arrow or Settings. Separate titles splits the group after dropping; it requires Timeline Helper Accessibility access on each Mac.
  • A more reliable Timeline Helper — The helper waits for Final Cut’s menu command to become available before separating. If it cannot finish, it closes the menu and explains how to retry without changing unrelated clips. English Final Cut menus are currently required.
  • Set up and retry — Open Set Up Timeline Helper in Settings to check the helper on this Mac. Select the tagged caption group and use Finish selected CaptionForge drop to retry.
  • Your zoom stays put — Drop your captions as one group and place them once. If Timeline Helper has to zoom to fit while it splits them into editable titles, it returns to your previous zoom afterwards. Turn this off in Settings.
  • Update the same extension — The installer replaces CaptionForge and its Final Cut extension together. Close Final Cut before installing, then reopen it to load the new version.
  • Check updates directly — Check for Updates inside Final Cut opens the updater without opening another caption editor. Your captions, presets, settings and models stay in place.
  • A cleaner installation — Installation refreshes the extension in Applications and clears stale CaptionForge registrations, without deleting your saved work or development copies.
  • Return to Final Cut — Updates started from the extension can return you to Final Cut after you close What’s New. Version and update instructions are clearer in Settings.
  • Recognizable in Final Cut — CaptionForge now declares its own bundled logo for the Final Cut Extensions menu, matching the app and What’s New artwork.
  • More room to drag — The default window is taller, with extra bottom padding so the Captions ready area stays comfortably visible. Compact windows reserve space for the same controls.

Quit Final Cut before updating. Captions, settings and downloaded models are preserved.

item.title: CaptionForge 1.0.6
item.description:
Clearer controls, reliable caption timing and easier access to updates.

  • A cleaner workspace — New app icon and refreshed What’s New cards. Expanded windows keep their dark background and minimum size; Analyze lights up when media is ready.
  • Know when captions are ready — A clear Captions ready area shows when the export checks pass and you can drag to Final Cut. Completed analysis keeps word and caption counts visible.
  • Settings, version and updates — The gear beside Favorites shows your version, Check for Updates and What’s New. Release notes appear once after an update and can be reopened here.
  • Complete single-word timing — Single-word captions retain their stored word interval. Timing summary explains Final Cut frame rounding and flags intervals too short to export safely.
  • Clearer timeline handoff — Improved helper discovery, faster timeline lookup and stable checks for separated titles. Final Cut still inserts a group before the helper separates it; manual Break Apart remains available.

Quit Final Cut before updating. Captions, settings and downloaded models are preserved.
